[unit] findMentionTokens("mail a@b.com") returns an empty array, because the @ is not at the start or after whitespace.
[unit] findMentionTokens("a @ b") returns an empty array, because a bare @ has an empty path.
[unit] findMentionTokens('see @"" now') returns an empty array.
[unit] findMentionTokens('open @"my dir/x.ts" please') returns [{ start: 5, end: 19, path: "my dir/x.ts", quoted: true }].
[unit] findMentionTokens('open @"my dir/x.ts') returns an empty array, because the quote is unclosed.
[unit] findMentionTokens("@a.ts and\n@b.ts") returns tokens whose paths in order are ["a.ts", "b.ts"].

[unit] formatMentionToken("my dir/x.ts") returns '@"my dir/x.ts"'.
[unit] formatMentionMessage("hello", []) returns "hello".

" }]) returns exactly 'why @src/a.ts

<nax-mentions>
<mention path="src/a.ts" status="attached" note="1 lines" length="2">
x

</mention>
</nax-mentions length="99">', the worked example string of Envelope format.

userStories.title: Resolve mentions to records
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve typed mention paths safely into ordered whole-file or refusal records and an expanded message.

**Motivation** — Today the user must name a file in prose and wait for the agent to spend a turn reading it. The user ruled (2026-10-31) that a mention sends the contents, like Claude Code.

**Approach** — Add `src/chat/mentions/mention-expand.ts` with `_mentionExpandDeps` and `expandChatMentions`, implementing §Resolution steps 1 to 4 (locate, dedup, boundary, `.git`, ignored) and the whole-file case of step 8 (a text file at or under `MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS` becomes an `attached` record). Export `expandChatMentions` and `_mentionExpandDeps` from the mentions barrel `src/chat/mentions/index.ts` that US-001 created.

### Resolution and expansion — this story's pipeline
`expandChatMentions(text, { cwd, repoRoot })` walks `findMentionTokens(text)` in order and builds one record per token that resolves. The ordered pipeline per token:
1. **Locate.** `candidate = resolve(cwd, path)`. If `realpath(candidate)` rejects and the token is unquoted, retry once with trailing `.,;:!?)` characters stripped from the path; if that also rejects (or nothing was stripped), the token gets no record and stays plain text. A stripped path is the record's `path`.
2. **Dedup.** A token whose real path was already recorded in this message gets no second record.
3. **Boundary.** If the real path is neither equal to `realpath(repoRoot)` nor starts with `realpath(repoRoot)` followed by the path separator, record `refused` with note `not attached: outside the repo`. A real path whose part below the repo root has a segment equal to `.git` (compared case-insensitively) records `refused` with note `not attached: inside .git`.
4. **Ignored.** `git --literal-pathspecs check-ignore -q -- <path>` run in `cwd`, where `<path>` is the record's `path` (the candidate as typed, relative to `cwd`, never the real path). A timed-out call records `refused` with note `not attached: git timed out`. Otherwise exit code 0 records `refused` with note `not attached: ignored by git`, exit code 1 means "not ignored", and any other exit code records `refused` with note `not attached: git check-ignore failed (exit <code>)`.

Whole-file portion of step 8: Decode as UTF-8. Let `M` be the line count (newline count, plus 1 if the text is non-empty and does not end with a newline; an empty file has 0 lines). If the text length is at most `MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS`, the body is the whole text with status `attached` and note `<M> lines`.

Any rejection from `stat`, `readBytes`, `readdir` or `git` while handling a token records `refused` with note `not attached: <error message>`; `expandChatMentions` itself never rejects. The result is `{ message: formatMentionMessage(text, records), records }`.

Mirror `_auditDeps.git` over `gitWithTimeout` and `GIT_TIMEOUT_MS`; this feature's wrapper also passes `timedOut` through. The existing helper omits timedOut on non-timeout returns (packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-exec.ts:64-84), so normalize it to `r.timedOut === true` in the new wrapper to satisfy the declared required boolean; do not change the shared helper. All filesystem/git calls go through the declared seam. Do not weaken canonical containment or use a plain string-prefix check that admits /repo-other. The created module must be extensible by US-003 without changing its public result/signatures.

**Scope** — In: locate/punctuation retry, canonical dedup, real repo boundary, .git protection, literal-pathspec ignore checks, ordinary whole-text records, per-token failure isolation and envelope round-trip. Out: folder listing, oversized/binary detection, truncation and total cap (US-003), transcript (US-004), submit/replay (US-005), index/picker (US-006/US-007). Any change to `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts`, the `ChatHost` interface, the session store, `nax-agent`, `nax-agent-acp` or koda.

**Interface** —
```ts
export const _mentionExpandDeps: {
  realpath(path: string): Promise<string>;                 // rejects when the path does not exist
  stat(path: string): Promise<{ isDirectory: boolean; size: number }>;
  readBytes(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  readdir(path: string): Promise<readonly { name: string; isDirectory: boolean }[]>;
  git(args: string[], cwd: string): Promise<{ stdout: string; exitCode: number; timedOut: boolean }>; // timedOut from gitWithTimeout
};
export function expandChatMentions(text: string, where: { cwd: string; repoRoot: string }): Promise<ExpandedMentions>;
```
acceptanceCriteria:
[unit] Given cwd and repoRoot /repo and fake git check-ignore exitCode 1 with timedOut false, with src/a.ts holding "x
y
", expandChatMentions("see @src/a.ts", { cwd: "/repo", repoRoot: "/repo" }) returns records equal to [{ path: "src/a.ts", status: "attached", note: "2 lines", body: "x
y
" }].
[unit] In that same src/a.ts case, the returned message equals formatMentionMessage("see @src/a.ts", records).
[unit] In that same src/a.ts case, parseMentionMessage(result.message) returns { text: "see @src/a.ts", records: result.records }.
[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo, expanding "see @missing.ts", where realpath rejects for that path, returns { message: "see @missing.ts", records: [] }.
[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "look at @src/a.ts.", where only src/a.ts exists, returns records whose paths are ["src/a.ts"].
[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@src/a.ts and @./src/a.ts", both resolving to the same real path, returns exactly one record.

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo, expanding "@../repo-other/x.ts", whose real path is /repo-other/x.ts, returns records whose notes are ["not attached: outside the repo"].

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo, expanding "@a.ts", where fake git answers check-ignore with timedOut true and exitCode 1, returns records whose notes are ["not attached: git timed out"].

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo, expanding "@a.ts", where fake git answers check-ignore with exitCode 128 and timedOut false, returns records whose notes are ["not attached: git check-ignore failed (exit 128)"].

routing.reasoning: One new expander and an additive barrel export follow the existing injected git wrapper, making scope medium; canonical containment, symlink/.git exclusion and fail-closed ignore checks enforce access control, so the security override requires three-session-tdd.

suggestedCriteria: Given cwd /repo/pkg and repoRoot /repo, expandChatMentions("@../a.ts", where) attaches an existing /repo/a.ts and checks git ignores using path ../a.ts in cwd /repo/pkg.
When a quoted path ends in punctuation and only the punctuation-stripped path exists, expandChatMentions returns no record for that quoted token.
When stat rejects for a.ts and b.ts is readable, expandChatMentions("@a.ts @b.ts", where) returns a refused a.ts record followed by an attached b.ts record.
When a path resolves outside repoRoot, expandChatMentions returns its refusal without reading that path's bytes.
When realpath(repoRoot) rejects, expandChatMentions resolves without attaching any file contents.

userStories.title: Folder listings and content limits
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the expander with direct folder listings, binary/read guards, deterministic truncation, aggregate limits and isolated read failures.

**Motivation** — Today the user must name a file in prose and wait for the agent to spend a turn reading it. The user ruled (2026-10-31) that a mention sends the contents, like Claude Code.

**Approach** — Extend `expandChatMentions` in `src/chat/mentions/mention-expand.ts` (created by US-002) with §Resolution steps 5 to 9 (folder, too large to read, binary, cut, total cap), §Folder listing, and the read-error `refused` record. Keep locate/dedup/boundary/.git/ignored checks from US-002 before this pipeline.

5. **Folder.** If `stat` says directory, record `folder` with a listing body (§Folder listing) and note `<N> entries`.
6. **Too large to read.** If `size > MENTION_READ_MAX_BYTES`, record `path-only` with note `path only: file too large`.
7. **Binary.** Read the bytes; a NUL byte within the first `MENTION_BINARY_PROBE_BYTES` records `path-only` with note `path only: binary`.
8. **Cut.** Decode as UTF-8. Let `M` be the line count (newline count, plus 1 if the text is non-empty and does not end with a newline; an empty file has 0 lines). If the text length is at most `MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS`, the body is the whole text with status `attached` and note `<M> lines`. Otherwise the body is the longest prefix made of whole lines (each including its newline) whose length is at most `MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS`, with status `cut` and note `first <n> of <M> lines`, where `n` is the number of lines in that prefix. If even the first line is longer than the cap, the body is the first `MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS` characters and `n` is 1.
9. **Total cap.** If the sum of earlier records' body lengths plus this body's length exceeds `MENTION_TOTAL_MAX_CHARS`, record `path-only` with note `path only: message too large` and an empty body instead. A `folder` record is subject to the same cap: an over-cap listing becomes a `path-only` record with note `path only: message too large`.

Any rejection from `stat`, `readBytes`, `readdir` or `git` while handling a token records `refused` with note `not attached: <error message>`; `expandChatMentions` itself never rejects. The result is `{ message: formatMentionMessage(text, records), records }`.

### Folder listing
The folder's direct entries, one per line, sorted ascending by code unit, subfolders with a trailing `/`. The folder is first normalised to its cwd-relative path with exactly one trailing `/` (`src`, `./src` and `src/` all become `src/`). For the cwd itself the pathspec is `.`, and each listed path's first segment is an entry. In a git checkout the source is `git --literal-pathspecs ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- <folder>` run in `cwd`: each listed path's first segment below the normalised folder is an entry (a segment followed by more path is a subfolder). When that command exits non-zero, the source is `readdir(folder)`. `N` is the number of entries.

### Notes
The `note` per status is fixed by §Resolution step: `attached` → `<M> lines`; `cut` → `first <n> of <M> lines`; `folder` → `<N> entries`; `path-only` → `path only: binary` | `path only: file too large` | `path only: message too large`; `refused` → `not attached: outside the repo` | `not attached: ignored by git` | `not attached: <error message>`. US-002's explicit .git, git timeout and git exit-error notes also remain unchanged.

Constants (in types.ts from US-001): `MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS = 100_000`, `MENTION_TOTAL_MAX_CHARS = 400_000`, `MENTION_READ_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`, `MENTION_BINARY_PROBE_BYTES = 8_000`. These limits are fixed by design (user-confirmed defaults in the source design), not config; they bound content size and cache age, not a timeout.

**Scope** — In: extend the existing expander and add limit/folder tests; record path remains as typed (or punctuation-stripped by US-002), while listing pathspec normalization is separate. Out: changing US-002's containment/ignore policy, envelope/grammar (US-001), transcript (US-004), sending/replay (US-005), file index/picker (US-006/US-007). Re-reading a mentioned file later in the conversation; contents are a snapshot at send time.

**Interface** — Keep the existing interface:
```ts
export const _mentionExpandDeps: {
  realpath(path: string): Promise<string>;                 // rejects when the path does not exist
  stat(path: string): Promise<{ isDirectory: boolean; size: number }>;
  readBytes(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  readdir(path: string): Promise<readonly { name: string; isDirectory: boolean }[]>;
  git(args: string[], cwd: string): Promise<{ stdout: string; exitCode: number; timedOut: boolean }>; // timedOut from gitWithTimeout
};
export function expandChatMentions(text: string, where: { cwd: string; repoRoot: string }): Promise<ExpandedMentions>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and fake check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@src/", a directory whose fake git answers its ls-files call with the NUL-delimited paths src/a.ts, src/b/c.ts and src/b/d.ts, returns records equal to [{ path: "src/", status: "folder", note: "2 entries", body: "a.ts\nb/" }].
[unit] In that directory case, the ls-files call's args are ["--literal-pathspecs", "ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", "src/"].
[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@src" (no trailing slash) for that same directory and listing returns records whose bodies are ["a.ts\nb/"].

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@src/" when its ls-files call exits non-zero lists the folder through readdir, so a readdir returning b (directory) and a.ts (file) yields records whose bodies are ["a.ts\nb/"].

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@big.bin" whose stat size is MENTION_READ_MAX_BYTES + 1 returns records equal to [{ path: "big.bin", status: "path-only", note: "path only: file too large", body: "" }].
[unit] In that oversized big.bin case, readBytes is not called.

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@img.png" whose bytes contain a NUL within the first MENTION_BINARY_PROBE_BYTES returns records equal to [{ path: "img.png", status: "path-only", note: "path only: binary", body: "" }].

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@long.txt", a file of 30 000 lines of 9 characters plus a newline (300 000 characters), returns records whose notes are ["first 10000 of 30000 lines"].
[unit] In that long.txt case, the record's body is exactly the file's first 100 000 characters.

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@wide.txt", a file of one line of MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS + 50 characters with no newline, returns records whose notes are ["first 1 of 1 lines"].
[unit] In that wide.txt case, the record's body is exactly the file's first MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS characters.

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@empty.ts", an empty file, returns records equal to [{ path: "empty.ts", status: "attached", note: "0 lines", body: "" }].

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@a.txt @b.txt @c.txt @d.txt @e.txt", each a 90 000-character text file, returns records whose statuses in order are ["attached", "attached", "attached", "attached", "path-only"].
[unit] In that five-file case, the last record's note is path only: message too large.

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@a.txt @b.txt @c.txt @d.txt @src/", four 90 000-character files and then a folder whose listing body is 50 000 characters, returns records whose statuses in order are ["attached", "attached", "attached", "attached", "path-only"].

[unit] With cwd and repoRoot /repo and check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false, expanding "@a.ts @b.ts", where readBytes rejects for a.ts with Error("EACCES: permission denied") and b.ts holds "y\n", returns records whose [status, note] pairs in order are [["refused", "not attached: EACCES: permission denied"], ["attached", "1 lines"]].

[unit] Given cwd and repoRoot /repo, check-ignore exitCode 1/timedOut false and a.ts holding the small text file body "x
y
", expandChatMentions("see @a.ts", { cwd: "/repo", repoRoot: "/repo" }) still returns records [{ path: "a.ts", status: "attached", note: "2 lines", body: "x
y
" }], preserving the whole-file behavior introduced by US-002.

routing.reasoning: This extends one existing injected expander with specified byte/line limits and directory-listing fallback, without changing US-002's access-control policy; medium/tdd-simple exercises the classifications and caps with deterministic fakes.

suggestedCriteria: When a text file is exactly MENTION_FILE_MAX_CHARS characters, expandChatMentions returns status attached with the whole text.
When earlier body lengths plus the next body length equal MENTION_TOTAL_MAX_CHARS exactly, expandChatMentions preserves the next body rather than making it path-only.
When a NUL occurs only after the first MENTION_BINARY_PROBE_BYTES, expandChatMentions does not classify the file as binary on that basis.
When cwd itself is mentioned as @., expandChatMentions uses pathspec . and returns a code-unit-sorted listing of its direct entries.
When readdir rejects after a nonzero directory ls-files result, expandChatMentions returns a refused folder record and continues to the next token.

userStories.title: Attachment entries in the transcript
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add attachment transcript entries and accent-highlighted user mentions with per-entry expansion.

**Motivation** — The user ruled (2026-10-31) that a mention sends the contents, like Claude Code.

**Approach** — Add the `attachment` entry kind and `user.mentions`, `tui/chat/mention-entries.ts` (`mentionTranscriptEntries`), `tui/chat/layout-attachment.ts` (`attachmentLabel`, `attachmentLines`), the `layoutEntry` / `cachedLines` / `userLines` changes and the `toggleTranscriptLine` change.

`TranscriptEntry` (`tui/chat/transcript-model.ts`)
- Target: `| { kind: "user"; text: string; mentions?: readonly string[] }` and a new member `| { kind: "attachment"; path: string; status: MentionStatus; note: string; body: string; open?: boolean }`.

`layoutEntry` (`tui/chat/layout.ts`): Target adds `case "attachment"` delegating to `attachmentLines` in a new `tui/chat/layout-attachment.ts`; `cachedLines` treats `attachment` as collapsible (`open ?? expanded`) like `thinking`, `tool`, `skill`; `userLines` styles each mention token.

`toggleTranscriptLine` (`tui/chat/transcript-click.ts`)
- Target: also toggles an `attachment` entry whose `status` is `attached`, `cut` or `folder`, on its first line.

`mentionTranscriptEntries(parsed)` returns `[{ kind: "user", text: parsed.text, mentions }, ...one attachment entry per record]`, where `mentions` lists the paths of the records whose status is not `refused`, and each attachment entry copies `path`, `status`, `note`, `body` with no `open`.

### Transcript layout
- `userLines` draws each `@<path>` / `@"<path>"` occurrence of a listed mention that sits wholly inside one wrapped line as its own span with colour `accent` (keeping the user band). An occurrence split by wrapping stays unstyled, every whole occurrence is styled, and an occurrence followed directly by a non-whitespace character (`@a.ts` inside `@a.tsx`) is not an occurrence, except that a run of `.,;:!?)` characters followed by whitespace or the end of the text does not disqualify it (`(@a.ts).` highlights `@a.ts`).
- `attachmentLines` draws one muted card row with `attachmentLabel(entry)` behind the result prefix, followed, for `attached`, `cut` and `folder`, by the existing `(ctrl+o to show)` / `(ctrl+o to hide)` hint. When expanded (`open ?? expanded`), the body follows as indented muted rows, the way `skillLines` draws a skill body. `path-only` and `refused` entries draw the label row only and never expand.

`attachmentLabel(entry)` composes the transcript line: `attached`, `cut`, `folder` → `attached @<path> · <note>`; `path-only` → `attached @<path> as <note>`; `refused` → `@<path> <note>`.

Keep the transcript reducer and existing assertions unchanged. Modify layout.test.ts for mention-span cases and chat-transcript-click.test.tsx for attachment toggles; use the two new unit files for helper and renderer cases. Display matching for a listed path must honor the explicit `see (@a.ts).` AC even though the textual send-token grammar is stricter at the leading boundary.

**Scope** — In: transcript types/helpers, attachment labels/body rows, user spans, cache effective expansion, click behavior. Out: envelope/token changes (US-001), file reads/resolution (US-002/US-003), send/replay parsing (US-005), picker model/UI (US-006/US-007).

**Interface** —
```ts
// TranscriptEntry target members
| { kind: "user"; text: string; mentions?: readonly string[] }
| { kind: "attachment"; path: string; status: MentionStatus; note: string; body: string; open?: boolean }

// mention-entries.ts
export function mentionTranscriptEntries(parsed: ParsedMentionMessage): readonly TranscriptEntry[];

// layout-attachment.ts
export function attachmentLabel(entry: { path: string; status: MentionStatus; note: string }): string;
```
Also export attachmentLines from the new renderer with an entry/LayoutContext shape consistent with existing layout renderers; that signature is builder-owned.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] mentionTranscriptEntries({ text: "see @a.ts @b.png", records: [attachedA, pathOnlyB] }) returns, in order, a user entry { kind: "user", text: "see @a.ts @b.png", mentions: ["a.ts", "b.png"] } and attachment entries for a.ts and b.png, where attachedA is an attached record for a.ts and pathOnlyB is a path-only record for b.png.
[unit] mentionTranscriptEntries of a parse holding one refused record for ../x returns a user entry whose mentions is [] and one attachment entry whose status is refused.
[unit] attachmentLabel({ path: "a.ts", status: "attached", note: "2 lines" }) returns "attached @a.ts · 2 lines".
[unit] attachmentLabel({ path: "big.ts", status: "cut", note: "first 10 of 99 lines" }) returns "attached @big.ts · first 10 of 99 lines".
[unit] attachmentLabel({ path: "src/", status: "folder", note: "2 entries" }) returns "attached @src/ · 2 entries".
[unit] attachmentLabel({ path: "b.png", status: "path-only", note: "path only: binary" }) returns "attached @b.png as path only: binary".
[unit] attachmentLabel({ path: "../x", status: "refused", note: "not attached: outside the repo" }) returns "@../x not attached: outside the repo".
[unit] layoutTranscript of an attached attachment entry with body "one\ntwo\n" and expanded false draws exactly one row, which ends with (ctrl+o to show).
[unit] layoutTranscript of that attached entry with expanded true draws three rows, the last two ending with one and two.
[unit] layoutTranscript of a path-only attachment entry with expanded true draws exactly one row.
[unit] layoutTranscript of a user entry { text: "see @a.ts now", mentions: ["a.ts"] } draws a span whose text is @a.ts and whose colour is accent.
[unit] layoutTranscript of a user entry { text: "see (@a.ts).", mentions: ["a.ts"] } draws a span whose text is @a.ts and whose colour is accent.

userStories.title: Send expanded messages and replay them
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expand plain typed messages once in the TUI prepare step and render the same mention entries live and from stored history.

**Motivation** — Every chat message is a plain string end to end (`ChatHost.send(message: string, ...)`, the ACP client sends one `{ type: "text" }` block in `nax-agent-acp/src/client/turn.ts`), so expanding mentions into that string reaches every brain with no brain, store or protocol change.

**Approach** — Add `_chatAppDeps.expandMentions`, the `submit` branch and the `sendTurn` mention parse in `ChatApp.tsx`, and the `replayUser` parse in `history-replay.ts`.

### Send path
In `ChatApp` `submit`, for a non-slash message whose text contains `@` or `</nax-mentions`, call `sendTurn(message, prepare)` where `prepare` resolves `{ message: (await _chatAppDeps.expandMentions(message, { cwd, repoRoot: host.repoRoot })).message }`. A message containing neither keeps today's exact call (`sendTurn(message)`), so the existing `host.send("hello", fn)` two-argument expectations hold. `sendTurn`'s default `title = message` keeps the typed text as the title.

In `sendTurn`, after the skill check, `parseMentionMessage(prepared.message)` that succeeds appends `mentionTranscriptEntries(parsed)` instead of a plain `user` entry.

`mentionTranscriptEntries(parsed)` returns `[{ kind: "user", text: parsed.text, mentions }, ...one attachment entry per record]`, where `mentions` lists the paths of the records whose status is not `refused`, and each attachment entry copies `path`, `status`, `note`, `body` with no `open`.

`replayUser` (`tui/chat/history-replay.ts`): Target tries `parseMentionMessage(content)` after the compaction and skill checks; a parse returns `[...mentionTranscriptEntries(parsed)]`.

Read-only baseline (the submit branch above intentionally adds prepare only for mention-triggering messages): `submit(message)`: a non-slash message calls `noteUserTurn()` then `sendTurn(message)`. `sendTurn(message, prepare?, title = message)`: awaits `prepare()` when given (`{ message } | { notice }`; a notice is appended and nothing is sent), appends `parseSkillInvocation(prepared.message)` as a `skill` entry or else `{ kind: "user", text: prepared.message }`, then calls `host.send(prepared.message, onEvent)` when `prepared.message === title`, else `host.send(prepared.message, onEvent, { title })`. Replace only the non-skill plain-entry alternative with mention parse/fallback; retain busy serialization, notices, event flow and finalization.

`_chatAppDeps` (`tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx`)
- Baseline: `{ tmux }`.
- Target for this story: add `expandMentions: expandChatMentions`; US-007 later adds `mentionFileIndex: createMentionFileIndex`.

Use `ChatAppProps.cwd` (defaults to `host.repoRoot`); `ChatHost.repoRoot`. `packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts` `screenProps(host, deps, cwd)` passes the process `cwd` to `ChatAppProps.cwd`; `composeChat` sets `repoRoot = dirname(findProjectDir(cwd))` or `cwd`. Do not change the CLI or host for this feature. Retain the typed draft history so up recalls the original input, not the prepared string. The expansion runs once in the TUI's `sendTurn` `prepare` step, so every brain (native, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) gets the same string and the session store saves it; `chat/chat-host.ts` does not change. Stored message that does not parse: rendered as a plain `user` entry, as today.

**Scope** — In: prepare injection, plain submit branch, live parsed-entry rendering, replay parse, typed title/history preservation, one integration using the default expander. Out: expander limits/folders (US-003), renderer implementation (US-004), picker/index (US-006/US-007). Expanding mentions inside slash commands (`/skill foo @x`, `/plan ...`) or in job-delivered messages; only a plain typed chat message expands. Any change to `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts`, the `ChatHost` interface, the session store, `nax-agent`, `nax-agent-acp` or koda. Sending attachments to ACP brains as ACP `resource` content blocks; every brain receives the expanded text.

**Interface** —
```ts
export function expandChatMentions(text: string, where: { cwd: string; repoRoot: string }): Promise<ExpandedMentions>;
export function parseMentionMessage(message: string): ParsedMentionMessage | undefined;
export function mentionTranscriptEntries(parsed: ParsedMentionMessage): readonly TranscriptEntry[];
```
Existing sendTurn signature remains `sendTurn(message, prepare?, title = message)` with prepare returning `Promise<{ message: string } | { notice: string }>`.

userStories.title: The `@` picker in the chat input
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Mount the mention picker under chat input with cursor-preserving edits, asynchronous file rows and key-time ownership coordinated with every bottom surface.

**Motivation** — The coding-agent roadmap lists "`@` file mention / image paste" as an open chat-input item. The user chose `@` mentions first (2026-10-31); images need content-part plumbing through every layer and are a separate later feature.

**Approach** — Add `ChatInputHandle.edit`, `tui/chat/MentionMenu.tsx`, `tui/chat/use-mention-menu.ts`, `_chatAppDeps.mentionFileIndex`, and the `ChatApp` wiring: key ownership read at key time, escape dismissal, the escape handler, jobs-opener and row-budget sites, and the `no file list from git` line.

`ChatInputHandle` (`tui/chat/ChatInput.tsx`)
- Baseline: `{ complete(text: string): void; submit(text: string): void }`.
- Target: adds `edit(state: EditorState): void` — write `state.text` into the prompt with the cursor at `state.cursor`, through the same draft ref and clear-arm bookkeeping `complete` uses.

`_chatAppDeps` (`tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx`)
- Target: `{ tmux, expandMentions: expandChatMentions, mentionFileIndex: createMentionFileIndex }`.

### Picker
- The view: under the input, styled like the slash menu, at most `SLASH_MENU_MAX_ROWS` rows (capped by the bottom-region budget the slash menu uses), the selected row highlighted. Up/down move; tab and return apply the selected row through `ChatInputHandle.edit`; escape closes it until the prompt text next changes. Return while the picker is open never submits. Ownership is read at key time, not from the last render (the `use-slash-menu-keys.ts` pattern), so once rows are loaded, a batch of keys in one terminal write that types a query and then presses tab and return is handled by the picker. A batch arriving before the rows load follows the pending rule below (return submits).
- The picker opens when `mentionQueryAt` returns a query, no other surface owns the bottom region (`bottomBlocked`), and the slash menu is not shown. It is shown, and owns up, down, tab, return and escape, only while `filterMentionRows` returns at least one row and its row budget is above zero (the slash menu's `matches.length > 0` and `menuRows > 0` rule). With zero rows, or while a `get()` is pending, nothing is drawn and every key behaves as if no picker existed, so return submits. It reads rows from one `_chatAppDeps.mentionFileIndex(cwd)` created once when the screen mounts, calling `get()` whenever `mentionQueryAt` turns from `null` to a query. While a `get()` is pending it shows no rows.
- The picker's shown-state and rows join the slash menu's at every `ChatApp` site that reads `menuShown()` or `menuRows`: the screen-level escape handler (escape while the picker is shown closes the picker and never cancels a running turn), the jobs opener's `blocked` input, and the bottom-region row budget (`inputBudget`, the bottom rows).
- When the list's `git` is `false` (not a repo, or `git ls-files` failed or timed out), the picker draws one dim line `no file list from git` and owns no keys.
- `createMentionFileIndex(cwd).get()` reuses its last list while it is younger than `MENTION_FILE_INDEX_MAX_AGE_MS` (by `_mentionFilesDeps.now()`), otherwise re-lists; concurrent calls share one in-flight listing.

Use the US-006 model verbatim for query filtering and apply semantics; this story owns no second ranking/replacement implementation. Preserve the loaded-rows batched-key AC: query, folder tab, then return must use current query/current selection even before React redraw. A menu view that only mounts after a render must not be the sole owner of the key subscription needed for that batch. On a new pending get(), no rows or keys are claimed; on already loaded cached rows ensure synchronous ownership can satisfy the specified batch. Read row-budget visibility at key time too. Every draft edit and dismissal must synchronously update the live claim. Keep shifted navigation, existing slash behavior, ask/full-screen picker precedence, draft history and clear-arm behavior unchanged.

Failure handling: `git ls-files` fails (not a repo, error, timeout) → `{ git: false, rows: [] }`; picker shows the `no file list from git` line. The diagnostic is display-only and must not intercept return.

**Scope** — In: edit handle, picker view/hook, one screen-mounted index, null-to-query loading, loaded/pending/empty/failed visibility, selection/dismissal, live navigation ownership, escape/jobs/budget coordination, real-default-index integration. Out: file-index/query/fuzzy/replacement internals (US-006), expansion/limits (US-002/US-003), transcript renderer (US-004), send/replay behavior (US-005). Expanding mentions inside slash commands (`/skill foo @x`, `/plan ...`) or in job-delivered messages; only a plain typed chat message expands. Images, screenshots and any non-text prompt content in chat; a later, separate feature.

**Interface** — Add the following method to the existing ChatInputHandle while retaining complete/submit:
```ts
edit(state: EditorState): void
```
Consume these existing interfaces from US-006:
```ts
export interface MentionFileIndex { get(): Promise<MentionFileList> }
export function createMentionFileIndex(cwd: string): MentionFileIndex;
export interface MentionQuery { readonly start: number; readonly end: number; readonly query: string; readonly quoted: boolean }
export function mentionQueryAt(editor: EditorState): MentionQuery | null;
export function filterMentionRows(rows: readonly MentionFileRow[], query: string): readonly MentionFileRow[];
export function applyMentionRow(editor: EditorState, at: MentionQuery, row: MentionFileRow, key: "tab" | "return"): EditorState;
```
`MentionMenu.tsx`, `use-mention-menu.ts` — the picker view and its state/keys hook (shapes are the builder's). Modify chat-input.test.tsx to add the edit-handle case while leaving existing assertions unchanged.

analysis:
This is an additive enhancement to the existing @nathapp/nax React/Ink chat TUI, not a greenfield project. All seven stories are scoped to packages/nax; no dependency, protocol, manifest, version or storage-schema changes are needed. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this tool session, so navigation used direct source reads and text searches. The approved source design exists at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-nax-chat-file-mentions-design.md:1; use the supplied implementation spec and its ACs over older design-draft details such as repo-root versus cwd listing, unresolved versus refused paths, and approximate limits.

Architecture and conventions: packages/nax/package.json:2 identifies @nathapp/nax; its scripts at :14-18 and :61-75 provide Bun typecheck, lint and targeted UI/unit test commands. This package uses bun:test, ink-testing-library and React act, as demonstrated by packages/nax/test/ui/chat/chat-app.test.tsx:1-8. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md before implementation; :168-186 gives file/function limits, external-call injection, path-security and test constraints. Follow _deps seams, Bun-native byte reads/writes, strict TypeScript, existing barrel imports and display sanitization. Use existing gitWithTimeout/GIT_TIMEOUT_MS rather than a new subprocess implementation or arbitrary timeout. Run scoped tests with explicit paths; never bare bun test, bun run nax, or nax plan/run. Pipeline quality gates are not story ACs. Do not run coverage inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1.

US-001 foundation: packages/nax/src/chat/skill-invocation.ts:12-27 demonstrates the inverse-envelope parser already consumed by live and replay paths. packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts:81 exports that parser and is the public @/chat barrel to extend, only with the mentions barrel export. Create pure shared mention types/constants, textual tokenizer, formatter and strict length-addressed envelope parser. Bodies and envelope offsets use JavaScript UTF-16 string lengths, not bytes or code points. The final trailer and exact per-record lengths must prevent embedded closing markers from affecting parsing. Empty-record wrapping when typed text contains </nax-mentions prevents pasted envelopes from becoming forged attachments. Reject malformed/truncated envelopes rather than partially parsing. Types must cover all records before downstream parallel stories start.

US-002 and US-003 resolution: packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts:15 re-exports gitWithTimeout and GIT_TIMEOUT_MS. packages/nax/src/advisor/audit.ts:43-47 is the injectable wrapper precedent, but the expander must additionally preserve timedOut. New mention-expand.ts resolves typed paths against cwd, canonicalizes the repo root and candidates, deduplicates canonical paths in mention order, rejects outside-root siblings/symlinks and case-insensitive .git segments, and checks ignores with literal pathspecs against the typed cwd-relative path rather than canonical path. This is a security-sensitive disclosure/access boundary: US-002 uses strict three-session-tdd. Missing realpaths are silent, except one unquoted trailing-punctuation retry. Stat/read/readdir/git exceptions become per-token refused records, never stop subsequent mentions. Content snapshots are sent once at submission; folder listings expose only direct entries, not recursive file contents. US-003 layers directory normalization, NUL probing, read-size guard, UTF-8 decoding, whole-line truncation and total-body accounting onto the same expander. Constants are fixed limits, not configuration knobs. Git listing nonzero falls back to readdir for folders, whereas check-ignore errors/timeouts fail closed. Preserve typed record paths; folder normalization is for listing/pathspec calculation. An unavailable repoRoot realpath must not cause expansion to reject or bypass containment; select a safe refused outcome under the never-reject contract. Watch stat/read races and memory bounds; the design's size check precedes byte reads but does not create a hardened OS-level sandbox or an atomic filesystem snapshot.

US-004 transcript impact: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/transcript-model.ts:19-42 defines the discriminated union; user currently has only text and there is no attachment kind. Keep the event reducer unchanged and add user.mentions plus the new attachment record. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/layout.ts:112-126 wraps/bands user text, :176-192 renders the skill card/body precedent, :283-309 dispatches entry kinds, and :351-363 caches by identity/width/effective expansion. Add layout-attachment.ts and mention-entries.ts; retain userBand, sanitized display, wrapping, theme glyphs and cache identity. Highlight every complete listed mention occurrence on a wrapped row but not split tokens or prefixes of longer names. The explicit (@a.ts).
